newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Anthrax kills two in Ukraine, infects 29 more.
newsitem.headline: Anthrax kills two in Ukraine, infects 29 more.

text.p: Anthrax has killed a husband and wife and infected 29 more people in Ukraine, a senior doctor said on Thursday, in an outbreak which local media blamed on meat given to workers instead of wages.

The disease, whose victims suffer nausea, a raging temperature, festering boils and die in agony, spread after farm workers were given meat from animals which died in a sudden outbreak of "cattle plague", the respected Den daily said.

"We have not done all the checks but the preliminary diagnosis of the dead couple is that they had anthrax," said Anatoly Grenevich, deputy chief doctor of the main hospital in Volnovakha in the southern coalmining region of Donetsk.
The lives of the 29 sick people diagnosed with anthrax were not in danger and the outbreak was under control, Grenevich told Reuters by telephone.
The dead couple, in their early 40s, died last week but their two teenage daughters were free of the disease, he said.
If anthrax is treated promptly patients can be cured.
Den quoted a local administration official as saying the workers had been given the meat instead of wages to tide them over a week-long national holiday this month.
A post-communist cash crisis in Ukraine means many workers often receive food or other goods instead of pay.
The paper said the infected meat had found its way to 28 points of sale. But the health ministry said all the meat had since been retrieved.
"One tonne and 200 kgs of infected meat was sold but it was quickly tracked down and stopped," Anatoly Voloshin, who heads the health ministry's press office in Kiev, said.
Diseases virtually unheard of in the West like cholera and dysentery have hit Ukraine and other former Soviet republics where sanitary rules are lax and medical structures drastically short of funds.
But anthrax, which is so deadly it is used in biological weapons, is extremely rare.
